hook.text: You hire someone to manage your money. They invest it where they earn the biggest commission, not the best return.

buildup.text: The agency problem occurs when managers' interests diverge from those of the shareholders who employ them.

discovery.text: Stock options were meant to align interests. Instead, they incentivized short-term stock manipulation.

twist.text: CEOs boosted stock prices with buybacks to cash their options, even as long-term value eroded.

climax.text: Every governance mechanism tries to solve the agency problem. None have fully succeeded.

punchline.text: Hire someone to serve your interests. They serve theirs.

quiz.question: What is the agency problem?
options: Managers pursue their own interests over shareholders'
Too many agencies regulate one company
Agents refuse to manage any company
